newsitem.title: USA: WALL ST WEEK AHEAD/New Year to test sentiment.
newsitem.headline: WALL ST WEEK AHEAD/New Year to test sentiment.

text.p: Wall Street will suffer from a split personality this week, as the New Year provides a demarcation line for stock market sentiment.
Analysts expect equities to continue last week's rally rise in the early part of the week, then suffer a decline as investors begin to worry whether the economy will overheat.

"This week looks like it might a little bit more exciting," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany. "We're going to start to see what the economy did in December, and the pace in bonds and stocks could quicken quite a bit."
The Dow Industrials index rose for the second week in a row last week, confirming the Santa Clause theory that stocks rally nearly every year during Christmas.
"The first part of the week will be a continuation of last week, not up big, but more money will be drifting into the market," said Alfred Kugel, investment strategist at Stein Roe.
Portfolio managers will use the last days of the year to add big-capitalization stock holdings as a way to beef up full-year returns.

"After the first of the year, the incentive for people (to buy) will disappear, and we could see some softness and profit taking," said Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyon & Ross.

The week will be relatively light on economic data. On Monday, the Conference Board issues data on leading indicators for November, with the forecast at up 0.1 percent, versus up 0.1 percent in October.
On Thursday, the National Association of Purchasing Management will release the December report, with the forecast at 51.5 compared to 52.7 in November.

"Both will give us a strong sense of what happened in the economy in December," said Johnson of First Albany. "We have a hint that it weakened...and the NAPM report could confirm it. They will be watched very carefully."

Analysts said the market has been benefiting from a healthy economy. "We're still in that Goldilocks economy, growing moderately -- not too strong and not too weak," said Kugel of Stein Roe. "There's not any significant likelihood that the Federal Reserve will tighten rates. The economy is positive, and money needs to be invested."

The presence of New Year's Day on Wednesday will impart some tranquillity to the week. "There will be an absence of research recommendations," said Eric Miller, chief investment officer at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette. "There's also the absence of new issues. The supply is a little lighter than it might normally be."
